spec.prompt: Deep snow in the Ural taiga, grey late-afternoon light, snow falling. The scorched dark spherical Voskhod-2 capsule (first reference) lies in waist-deep snow. Its round hatch cover has been blown partly open but is jammed against the trunk of a large pale birch tree right beside the capsule, leaving only a narrow gap. Through the gap two pairs of hands in white spacesuit gloves push the hatch cover rhythmically back and forth against the birch, the whole capsule rocking a little with each heave, snow sliding off the branches. Between heaves the bare head and white spacesuit shoulder of the commander Pavel Belyayev (reference) appear in the gap as he shoves. Locked-off medium-wide shot, the hatch and the tree clearly readable. Photorealistic, shot on 35mm film, documentary realism. March 1965, the Ural taiga of Perm Oblast: dense snow-covered spruce and pale birch forest, waist-deep snow, breath steaming at -25 C. A red-orange-and-white parachute hangs snagged in the treetops. Accurate 1965 Soviet details only: no modern clothing or gear, no orange coveralls, no helmets. Clear readable subjects, uncluttered frame. No on-screen text, no captions.
